question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, Managing Partner of 'Arya Buyout Partners', is explaining to her IC why a buyout is structurally different from a plain-vanilla private equity investment. Which of the following is the ESSENTIAL distinction?

answer.text: A buyout targets primary share issuance for growth capital, while PE targets secondary shares
A buyout involves only debt financing while PE involves only equity financing
A buyout is restricted to listed companies while PE is restricted to unlisted companies
A buyout seeks control via secondary shares, while PE subscribes to primary shares for growth capital

explanation.text: The Logic: A buyout seeks control — usually 51% or more — by acquiring secondary shares from existing controlling shareholders. Private equity, by contrast, provides growth capital by subscribing to primary shares issued by the company and does not seek control. The Trap: Option A inverts primary and secondary. Option B is the trap — it confuses debt-only financing with the definition of a buyout; financing mix is a separate dimension from the control/share-source distinction. Option C is false — buyouts can target both listed and unlisted companies. Note: The two clean dimensions to remember are: (i) primary vs secondary shares and (ii) growth-capital vs control.
